text: In Ayodhya, King Dasharatha had four sons. The eldest, Rama, was brave, gentle, and true to his word.
asr: In Iodia, King Dasharatha had four sons. The eldest Rama was brave, gentle and true to his word.

text: In Mithila, Princess Sita would marry whoever could string the mighty bow of Shiva. Rama lifted it, and it snapped in two.
asr: In Matilla, Princess Sita would marry whoever could string the mighty bow of Shiva. Rama lifted it, and it snapped in two.

text: But on the eve of his crowning, Queen Kaikeyi claimed two old promises: her son Bharata as king, and Rama exiled for fourteen years.
asr: But on the eve of his crowning, Queen Kaikai claimed two old promises. Her son Barata as king and Rama exiled for 14 years.

text: Rama left without anger. Sita and his brother Lakshmana walked beside him.
Bharata would not take the throne. He placed Rama's sandals upon it, and waited.
asr: Barata would not take the throne. He placed Rama's sandals upon it and waited.

text: In the forest, a golden deer appeared. Rama chased it, but it was a demon in disguise.
Then Ravana, king of Lanka, seized Sita in his flying chariot. The brave vulture Jatayu fought him, and fell.
asr: Then Ravana, King of Lanka, seized Sita in his flying chariot. The brave vulture Jaddu fought him and fell.

text: Searching for her, Rama found friends: the monkey king Sugriva, and Hanuman.
asr: Searching for her, Rama found friends, the Monkey King Sugrava and Hanuman.

text: Hanuman leapt across the sea, gave Sita Rama's ring, and set Lanka ablaze with his burning tail.
asr: Hanuman leapt across the sea, gave cedar Rama's ring, and set Lanka ablaze with his burning tail.

text: The army built a bridge of floating stones, each one marked with Rama's name.
After a long war, Rama's arrow struck Ravana down, and Sita was free.
asr: After a long war, Ramas Arro struck Ravana down and Sita was free.

text: They came home to Ayodhya, where every road was lit with lamps, and Rama was crowned at last.
asr: They came home to Iodia, where every road was lit with lamps, and Rama was crowned at last.

text: Every Diwali, those lamps are lit again.
asr: Every Duwali, those lamps are lit again.

text: Rama: the one who kept his word.
